source_metadata.exact_title: Montelukast in hospitalized patients diagnosed with COVID-19

workflow.batching: single semantic pass; 7-page source did not require large-source batching

source_consistency_findings: Table 5 contains internally inconsistent percentages for several ordinal-scale delta categories relative to the displayed counts (for example, 1/30 shown as 0%, 26/30 as 84%, 3/30 as 12%). Primary clinical-deterioration counts/rates are internally consistent.
Azithromycin imbalance is reported as p=0.01 in Table 2 and p=0.009 in the Results narrative; the table-anchored atom preserves p=0.01 and is tagged source-inconsistency.
Discussion cites “(1,23)” although the reference list contains only references 1-22; no reference 23 is available in the source PDF.

extraction_limitations: This observational study does not report treatment-emergent adverse-event data; no adverse_event atom was created from general montelukast safety discussion.
Sensitivity analyses for patients without asthma and without azithromycin report percentages but not subgroup denominators in the text; subgroup atoms therefore do not invent sample sizes.
The steroid sensitivity analysis is qualitative in the source and lacks a quantitative result; it is represented as qualitative_result rather than subgroup_result.
Background claims attributed to cited literature were not reclassified as primary-study results from this cohort.
schema_gaps: The current QuantitativeResult model has one top-level estimate, so two-arm medians/proportions are preserved in arms and canonical_statement while the top-level estimate corresponds to the montelukast arm or reported effect measure as labeled.
The model has no dedicated field for per-arm IQRs; IQRs are preserved in canonical_statement/original_result_text for length of stay.
